context:
Goal: a lane can fix its own commit on its own branch without stray branches.
Problem (rule): auto mode's classifier refuses `git push --force-with-lease` to a lane's own branch, yet the force-push guard names that push as the remedy. Two lanes hit it tonight (opus-plain-ask, call-judge-widening); each made a new branch and left a stale one, which the cloud cannot delete.
Based on (incident): debt note classifier-refuses-lease-push; closed draft #1191; stale branch opus-plain-ask.
Departs from: main, where auto mode refuses every force push — a adds an allow rule for a lease push to the session's own claude/ lane branch only.

options.gain: No stray branches; a commit can be fixed in place.
options.how: Add one auto-mode allow rule: `git push --force-with-lease` to the session's own claude/ lane branch only. The push guard still checks the branch. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.
options.label: Allow a lease push to the session's own claude/ branch
options.lose: A lease push to a wrong branch, made by mistake, passes the classifier; only the push guard stops it.

options.gain: The shared tool stays as it is.
options.how: No change; each fix goes on a new branch.
options.label: Keep the refusal
options.lose: Each fix leaves a stale branch for your computer to delete.

ref: note classifier-refuses-lease-push; closed draft #1191; stale branch opus-plain-ask
short: Lease push to own lane branch
title: Auto mode refuses a lane's force push to its own branch, so each fix leaves a stale branch. Allow that one form?
why: Recommended: b. Option a widens what a shared tool accepts. Meanwhile lanes keep making a new branch for each fix.
